task_brief: Day 3 of "Algorithms and Programming Structures" (unit 2, grade 7) is a guided practice on variables and data types. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Build a small interactive program and document tests, bugs, and revisions. Today's work contributes to that by handling variables and data types at the guided practice stage, against the unit's wider topics of decomposition, pseudocode, variables and data types, and conditionals. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Complete the first two test cases printed in activity_setup for variables and data types. On the first, work step by step with the printed method available, and after each step write the one-line reason that step is correct. On the second, work without the method in view and only check it after you commit to an answer. Both problems must show the intermediate states — a trace table, printed values, or a labelled diagram — not just a final result. Then state which of the two felt less certain and name the specific step where your confidence dropped. The activity_setup block below supplies the complete central input, exact specification, execution method, test cases, debugging target, and equal-credit manual simulation; use those exact materials rather than waiting for another handout, account, service, or tool. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about variables and data types, and it belongs to "Algorithms and Programming Structures", which also covers separate topics such as decomposition. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about variables and data types; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.

central_input.title: Inline variables and data types code case
central_input.purpose: Use this exact fictional case to investigate variables and data types; no other file, model, dataset, or account is needed.

expected_behavior_and_specification: The query must select active records and total their values; the supplied records must return 6.
Inactive records must not affect the result, and an empty record list must return 0.
The submitted explanation must connect the observed control flow or data state to variables and data types, not merely state the final number.
The smallest test case must be tried and its actual result compared with the expected result.

execution_method.primary: No-install browser method: open any browser developer console, paste the complete starter code, press Enter, and record the output or exact error text.
execution_method.local_optional: If Node.js is already installed, save the unchanged snippet as activity.js and run `node activity.js`; installing Node.js is not required.
execution_method.no_computer_required: The hand-trace route below is a complete execution method and earns identical credit.

debugging_target.observed_failure: The selection is correct, but the aggregation subtracts each selected value, so the supplied records return -6 instead of 6.
debugging_target.target: Repair the aggregation operator, explain the selected rows and accumulator state, and rerun all three tests.
debugging_target.passing_change: The reducer uses total + record.value; the tests return 6, 0, and 0.
debugging_target.scope_note: Diagnosing the state, control-flow, or data defect and connecting the repair to variables and data types is the central evidence.

equal_credit_alternative.method: Paper or notes-app simulation; this earns exactly the same score as running code.
steps: Make one row for each statement or loop check and copy the starting input exactly.
Record every variable, object field, selected item, and output after that step.
Circle the first row where the actual state stops matching the specification.
Apply the one repair named in your explanation and trace all three tests again.
equal_credit_alternative.evidence_to_submit: The completed trace, the one-line corrected condition, and an expected-versus-actual table for all three tests.

guided_scaffold_note: Scaffolding for variables and data types fades within the session: the first case may be worked with the reference, model, or prompts in view, and the second must be attempted before checking anything. The supporting adult may ask "what supports that move?" after a step but should not supply the step. Where the unscaffolded attempt diverges from the scaffolded one, the divergence itself is the thing to examine, not something to erase.
test_or_check_criteria: Both problems show intermediate states — trace table, printed values, or labelled diagram — not only final answers.
The first problem carries a per-step reason; the second was attempted before any reference was checked.
The step where confidence dropped is named specifically, not described as general uncertainty.
Every result is traceable to variables and data types or another named topic from this unit.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

remediation: Reteaching for variables and data types follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for variables and data types, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for variables and data types works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of variables and data types, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking variables and data types mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply variables and data types under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on variables and data types rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
